narrative.overview:
ModelView is a working inspection plate drawn in pure black and white, with one electric blue line for interaction and four defect inks for truth. The mesh is the specimen; the calibrated index rail holds the verdict, checks, measurements and objects; a defect never borrows the blue, so the accent can never be confused with a failure. The interface answers one question — is this printable? — in a single 44px reading before the eye reaches the detail.

The surface is black at every layer: viewport, top strip, rail, inspector and status bar are all #000000. Separation is earned by 1px #161E28 hairlines and #263545 interactive borders, never by tonal panel fills. The one blue (#2F6BFF) marks buttons, borders, focus, active segments, the selected-object rule and the hidden-inspector hint; it is the live line. Red #FF5A5F, amber #F5A524, teal #14B8A6 and violet #A78BFA mean open edge, non-manifold, flipped winding and degenerate — on the mesh, in the legend, and in the callouts.

The type ramp is deliberately larger than the first release for high-resolution displays: 76px wordmark, 44px verdict, 18px data, 15px row labels, 12.5px explanations, 11.5px metas, 10px rail labels. Density stays high because the content is dense; legibility comes first. The earlier charcoal/bone/sodium surface was retired at the user's request; the rail, callout and timing structures survive. Two opaque Blueprint sheets — Settings and Repair — extend the same plate: square radios and checkboxes, a filled Keep action (Send also fills when a slicer is configured), and a `REPAIRED PREVIEW` chip that becomes `REPAIRED` only after an explicit Keep.
keyCharacteristics: Pure #000000 field everywhere, with no tonal panel fills.
White primary text, blue-gray secondary; graphite-faint is decoration only.
One electric blue for interactive borders, buttons, focus and selection.
Four defect inks with fixed meanings, and darker line variants for the lit mesh.
Square hairlines, 0px corners, no shadows; the GPU mesh supplies the depth.
Condensed, tracked Archivo Narrow; a 44px verdict as the one display moment.
Real parse and check timings; no idle FPS.
Settings and Repair sheets are opaque black plates, not cards.
Repair is explicit: REPAIRED PREVIEW while previewing, REPAIRED after Keep; the source file is never overwritten.
Defect Theater is the one performance mode: one defect kind at a time, a ghost specimen, and a topology loupe.
No-wait large binary STL: a live flat mesh and six-cell analysis filmstrip appear before the authoritative report.
Orientation Adviser previews poses on an assumed 256³ bed; the source file and side report are never rewritten.
Large 3MFs that keep geometry in external parts offer FIX ON LOAD; recovery keeps plates/names and never rewrites the source.
Defined 3MF part colors replace the cool Clay palette; dark print colors are lifted for the black plate and swatched in object rows.

rules.name: The One Blue Rule
rules.body: #2F6BFF marks interactive state only: primary buttons, interactive borders, focus, active segments, selection. It is never a background, a heading color, or a defect ink.

rules.name: The Defect Ink Rule
rules.body: Red, amber, teal and violet mean open edge, non-manifold, winding and degenerate — in that binding, on the mesh and in the legend. They never decorate UI.

rules.name: The Pure Black Rule
rules.body: Every surface is #000000. Separation comes from a 1px hairline, never from a lighter panel fill.

rules.name: The Quiet Chrome Rule
rules.body: Content text is Graphite or White. Graphite Faint is reserved for ticks, disabled states and placeholder marks.

rules.name: The Small Type Rule
rules.body: In the loaded report, the smallest content is 10px (rail labels); explanations are 12.5px, metas 11.5px, row labels 15px, data 18px. Display type is the 44px verdict and the 76px wordmark; nothing else exceeds 18px.

rules.name: The Tracked Caps Rule
rules.body: Labels are uppercase, tracked 0.1–0.19em; body prose is never uppercase.

rules.name: The Fixed Chrome Rule
rules.body: The rail and inspector keep their widths. Only the viewport grows.

rules.name: The One Fold Rule
rules.body: The verdict, checks, and the first object/model group fit as far as the height allows; the rest scrolls behind a quiet blue-gray scrollbar.

rules.name: The Flat Plate Rule
rules.body: No box shadows, blur, glass or glow. A surface earns separation with a 1px line or a blue border.

rules.name: The Square Specimen Rule
rules.body: If a corner is visible, it is 0px. The one round content form is the defect callout; the settings gear is the only other circular glyph.

rules.name: The Explicit Repair Rule
rules.body: Repair is previewed on the real scene; Keep is the only way to mark REPAIRED, and the source file is never overwritten. A no-op preview says so and cannot be kept.

rules.name: The Safe Claim Rule
rules.body: The repair reports only the six safe passes, each validated against the real AFTER report. A non-manifold split is accepted only when it improves the report without opening new edges; declined passes stay visible. Deep remesh is a separate opt-in rebuild, never counted as a safe pass, and is offered only when the result is watertight. Self-intersections are not checked; the interface never implies otherwise.

rules.name: The Sheet Focus Rule
rules.body: Settings and Help dim the frame behind them; Repair dims the topbar, rail and inspector but keeps the live preview and status readout lit. The dim is a flat black scrim, never a shadow, blur or glass. When a centered sheet would clip the fixed topbar, status bar or inspector, that chrome yields to a blank field for the sheet’s lifetime; panel widths, the rail and the live preview stay put.

rules.name: The One Story Rule
rules.body: Theater holds one defect kind and one marker at a time. The focused kind keeps its ink at full strength; everything else becomes the ghost. Competing colored stories are forbidden.

rules.name: The Frame Is UI Rule
rules.body: The focus frame is 1px White with corner ticks; defect ink belongs to the geometry, and Electric Blue belongs to the interactive marker. Never paint a colored disc or halo around the focus.

rules.name: The No Aura Rule
rules.body: No bloom, glow, translucent disc, gradient or looping pulse. The ghost, the White frame, the ink lines and the topology loupe carry the moment.

rules.name: The No-Wait Rule
rules.body: A large binary STL must put geometry on screen before analysis finishes. The stream is flat and provisional; the analysis filmstrip and counts settle as the authoritative report lands. Never replace it with an indeterminate spinner.

rules.name: The Assumed Bed Rule
rules.body: Orientation is a 256 × 256 × 256 mm preview. The bed assumption is stated in the section and at the bed edge. The source file, source orientation and side report are never rewritten.

rules.name: The Recovered-Not-Rewritten Rule
rules.body: Recovery resolves external parts in memory, keeps plates and names, and skips broken parts. It never writes the source and never claims the mesh is watertight; Send exports a temporary recovered copy.

rules.name: The Defined Part Color Rule
rules.body: A 3MF's own part colors replace the cool palette. Dark print colors are lifted 32% toward white for the black plate; the object-row swatch shows the source color; undefined parts keep the Clay order. Color is per object, never invented per face. A warm part color is user content, not a sodium accent.

dos: Do keep every background at #000000; use 1px hairlines and blue borders for separation.
Do keep Electric Blue for interactive state only: buttons, borders, focus, active segments and selection.
Do keep the defect inks semantic on the mesh, in the legend and in the callouts; use the darker line variants on the lit mesh.
Do keep content text at Graphite or brighter; Graphite Faint is decoration only.
Do keep the larger ramp: 10px minimum for rail labels, 12.5px explanations, 15px rows, 18px data, 44px verdict.
Do keep 0px corners, 1px rules and no shadows.
Do follow BambuStudio for the viewport's hands and the Ctrl/Cmd+1–7 view presets.
Do show real parse and check timings; label synthetic samples and the STL millimetre assumption.
Do use opaque black sheets with a 1px Hairline Bright border and 0px corners; they are plates, not cards.
Do mark REPAIRED PREVIEW while previewing and REPAIRED only after Keep; disable Keep when no safe pass changed geometry.
Do state what repair did not heal; remaining non-manifold joins are reported, never claimed fixed.
Do label deep remesh as an opt-in rebuild and warn that detail may change.
Do ghost the specimen, not the defect; keep the focused kind in its ink and the rest of the field quiet.
Do use the White focus frame and the Blue selected-marker ring; no colored disc, halo or bloom.
Do keep the side report live in theater and return the camera on Esc.
Do stream large binary STL as a live flat mesh and let the six-cell filmstrip carry the analysis progress.
Do frame orientation as a preview on an assumed 256³ bed; rotate the specimen, never the source.
Do offer FIX ON LOAD when a large 3MF fails on external object parts, and keep every plate and object name after recovery.
Do use defined 3MF part colors in the viewport and object-row swatches; lift dark print colors for the black plate.
donts: Don't add eyebrow or kicker labels above headings; section locators live in the rail and the section heads.
Don't use a tonal panel fill to separate chrome from the viewport.
Don't use Electric Blue as a defect ink or as a decorative accent on data.
Don't use Graphite Faint for body, explanations, metas or state values.
Don't introduce cards, shadows, glass, gradients, pills or rounded corners.
Don't show idle FPS or invented performance numbers.
Don't use warm clay or sodium/warm-yellow accents; the surface is black, white and cool blue.
Don't put a second status stack beside the calibrated rail.
Don't claim every non-manifold join was healed or that self-intersections are detected; the safe repair is conservative.
Don't present deep remesh as safe or detail-preserving.
Don't overwrite the source file when saving or sending a repair.
Don't mark a scene repaired when the preview is unchanged.
Don't add particles, bloom, glow, chromatic aberration or idle loops to theater.
Don't let two defect kinds compete for the theater's ink at full strength.
Don't show a spinner for a large model when a streamed mesh can be visible.
Don't imply the orientation adviser changed the file or found a new defect fact.
Don't imply package recovery repaired the mesh; the checks and Repair flow still own that.
Don't invent per-face colors or override a defined part color with the Clay palette.
